context:
Establish a canonical TPC-DI ETL executor boundary first, then route both
SQL and DataFrame entry points through it. Keep mode-specific behavior limited
to connection acquisition and output envelope formatting.

Introduce a connection-provider protocol in core dataframe abstractions, update
adapters/contexts to satisfy it, and remove fallback/sniffing logic. Then add
parity tests that compare stage-level outcomes from SQL and DataFrame callers
under controlled fixtures.
description:
TPC-DI currently exposes separate execution paths for SQL and DataFrame modes,
and DataFrame mode discovers platform SQL connections via attribute sniffing.
This creates correctness risk (behavioral drift between modes), weakens
adapter contracts, and complicates future maintenance.

This TODO standardizes TPC-DI execution on one shared ETL orchestration path,
introduces an explicit connection-provider contract for DataFrame adapters,
and removes ambiguous API behavior in execute_dataframe_workload().

Scope focuses on runtime correctness and contract clarity for TPC-DI.

anti_patterns.dont: encode mode-specific semantics in shared ETL internals
anti_patterns.instead: isolate mode differences to thin adapters

anti_patterns.dont: keep separate ETL orchestration logic for SQL and DataFrame paths
anti_patterns.instead: route both through one shared executor

anti_patterns.dont: use hasattr/getattr sniffing for connection discovery
anti_patterns.why: adapter behavior is implicit and brittle

Existing TPC-DI benchmark metrics export structure remains backward-compatible for existing result consumers
TPC-DI transactional capability gating (transactions + incremental + SCD2) remains enforced before ETL stage execution
